name: Gala
rootCause: Possible hacker seized control of an admin address to mint a whopping 5 billion GALA tokens worth $216 million, rapidly offloading 592 million tokens for $21.8 million in ETH before Gala Games could blacklist the rogue address.

descriptions.text: Possible hacker seized control of an admin address to mint a whopping 5 billion GALA tokens worth $216 million, rapidly offloading 592 million tokens for $21.8 million in ETH before Gala Games could blacklist the rogue address.

An attacker gained control of a dormant MINTER-privileged wallet on the GALA token contract on Ethereum — a wallet that had not been used for approximately six months — by compromising its private key. On May 20, 2024, the attacker used this privileged account to mint 5 billion GALA tokens (nominally worth ~$219M at the time). The attacker swapped 592 million GALA for approximately 5,952 ETH (~$21.8M) via 0xProject before Gala Games' deployer added the exploiter's address to the contract's blocklist, roughly 2 hours and 16 minutes after the first mint. The remaining ~4.4 billion tokens were effectively frozen. The breach may have been facilitated by an insider — several Gala team members, including the President of Blockchain, departed three days before the exploit. The root cause was inadequate key management and lack of multi-sig controls over the privileged minter role. Attack Tx: 0xa6d90abe17d17743a9cecab84bcefb0fd0bbfa0c61bba60fd2f680b0a2f077fe Analysis: Explained: The Gala Games Hack (May 2024)

On May 20, 2024, the Web3 gaming platform Gala Games was attacked, resulting in a loss of approximately $21.8 million. The attacker minted 5 billion GALA tokens, worth over $200 million, and quickly sold 592 million GALA, receiving 5,952 ETH. On May 22, according to on-chain records and a statement from Gala Games on Discord, the digital wallet associated with the Gala Games hacker transferred 5,913.2 ETH, which was the hacker returning the stolen funds.

On May 20, 2024, Gala Games suffered an unauthorized mint of 5 billion GALA tokens on Ethereum by an attacker who gained control of a privileged minter/admin address through flawed access controls. Roughly 600 million tokens were sold for ETH, causing a swift 20% drop in GALA's price, while the remaining tokens were frozen and effectively burned. Gala Games contained the breach within 45 minutes and began collaborating with authorities. Compromise of a privileged minter/admin address enabled an unauthorized actor to mint GALA tokens.
